name: select_demo_scenario
description: Call this first, before you say anything, exactly once per call, with scenario set to 'deposit_short'. It prepares the account for this call. Never mention it or anything about setup to the caller, and never call it again.

name: authenticate_merchant
description: Call this after the caller gives their Merchant ID and the last four digits of the account their deposits go to, you've read both back one digit at a time, and the caller has said they're right. Pass merchant_id and bank_account_last4. The caller is verified only when the result contains authenticated: true; then say 'Thanks, you're verified. What can I help with?' If authenticated is false, ask once more for both values without saying which one didn't match; after a second failure, say you weren't able to verify them. If the result has tool_ran: false or an error, it's a system problem, not a failed try: call again with both values filled in. Never share anything about the account before verification.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID the caller said on this call and confirmed after you read it back. Never fill this in yourself.

bank_account_last4.description: The last four digits of the deposit account that the caller said on this call and confirmed after you read them back. Never fill this in yourself.

name: get_deposit_reconciliation
description: Call this when a verified caller says a deposit from a specific day is short or less than expected. Pass the day they named, such as 'Sunday'. Then say: 'I see it. Your card batches on {batch_day_spoken} totaled {batches_total}, and {deposited} was deposited. That's {difference} less, and all of it is accounted for:' then each cause in the order given, as '{amount} {explanation}'. Then, if holds is 'none', say 'Nothing is on hold.' and read any next_step exactly as written. Never do the math yourself, never reorder the causes, and never say anything from internal_do_not_say or internal terms like service type, conveyed, or SE number. If fully_explained is false, say part of the difference needs review.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

batch_date.description: The day the caller named: a weekday like 'Sunday', 'yesterday', or a date as YYYY-MM-DD.

name: get_disputes
description: Call this when a verified caller asks about a chargeback or what to do about one. Find the dispute matching the chargeback you mentioned. Say: 'The cardholder disputed a {amount} sale, and it's waiting for your response. {merchant_guidance} Disputes are time sensitive, so I'd send it as soon as you can.' If response_due_known is false, never state or estimate a deadline. Share merchant_guidance exactly as written and give no other evidence advice. Never say whether they will win.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: get_recent_deposits
description: Call this when a verified caller says they don't see a deposit, such as yesterday's. Find the batch for the day they mean using batch_date_relative_spoken. If its timing is 'not_yet_due', say: 'That one isn't late. Yesterday's sales are scheduled to reach your account {deposit_date_relative_spoken}.' (use the day they asked about in place of 'Yesterday's' if different). If timing is 'posted', tell them it was deposited on {deposit_date_spoken} to the account ending in {bank_account_last4}. Only if timing is 'late' treat it as missing and say a specialist will need to look into it.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: get_email_on_file
description: Call this only after a verified caller says yes to getting an email recap of the charges. Then read email_spoken back exactly as written and ask: 'I have {email_spoken} on file. Is that right?' Don't call send_recap_email until the caller says yes. If they say it's wrong, don't send; you can't change it on this call, so offer to connect them with the account changes team. If email_on_file is false, say there's no email on file and offer the account changes team. Never accept or use an email address the caller says.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

name: send_recap_email
description: Call this only after you've read the email on file from get_email_on_file to the caller and they've said it's right. It emails a recap of the deposit charges for that day to the address on file. Then say: 'Done. The recap is on its way to {to_spoken}.' Never read the email contents aloud. Call it once per call; if it returns already_sent, just say it's already on its way. If it returns an error, apologize and say you can't send it right now.

merchant_id.description: The Merchant ID from the successful authenticate_merchant result.

batch_date.description: The same day you used for get_deposit_reconciliation, such as 'Sunday', 'yesterday', or YYYY-MM-DD.

name: transfer
description: Call this to hand the caller to a team, only after the caller has said yes to being connected and you've said the handoff line out loud (for example 'Okay, connecting you with our disputes team now.'). Use disputes_chargebacks when the caller wants help responding to a chargeback. Use batch_transaction_deposit when a deposit is late, part of a difference needs review, or the caller asks for a person about their deposit. For anything outside deposits and chargebacks, use the matching team. Call it once; after it succeeds, stop talking.

queue.description: disputes_chargebacks: responding to a chargeback or dispute. batch_transaction_deposit: batch, transaction, or deposit questions, or a person about a deposit. statements_account_changes: statements, fees, tax documents, or account changes. terminal_support: terminal password, troubleshooting, paper supplies. voice_authorization: voice authorizations. government_public_sector: government or public sector customers.

reason.description: One line for the receiving team: whether the caller was verified, the Merchant ID and business name, what you found, and what the caller wants. Example: 'Verified 1234567 Example Shop; Sunday deposit short by chargeback; caller wants help responding.' Never include full card or bank account numbers.
